what: Marvell designs semiconductors for data infrastructure: the custom AI chips, optical connections, switches and storage controllers that move data inside and between data centres. It has no factories and uses TSMC to manufacture.
customers: Cloud providers and AI data centre operators, telecom equipment makers, enterprise networking vendors and carmakers.
money: custom AI silicon, optical interconnect and switching for cloud operators
chips for corporate networks and telecom infrastructure
moat: Deep engineering relationships with a handful of cloud customers who co-design chips with it, and leading expertise in high-speed optical interconnect.
risks: A few cloud customers account for much of revenue; losing one custom-chip socket matters a great deal
Broadcom is larger and competes directly for the same custom AI designs
Return on invested capital is low because of past acquisitions and amortisation
opportunities: Custom AI chips for cloud operators are growing much faster than the chip market as a whole
Optical interconnect demand rises with every new AI cluster built
Revenue grew about 42% in the last financial year as AI orders scaled
watch: Data centre revenue each quarter and any news on winning or losing a custom-silicon programme.
